correctness.rationale: The exact finding is true, including p=2, and matches Voll's Theorem 1, corollary, and local calculation. An independent way to check the prime-two issue is to take the abelianization exponents a≥b and commutator exponent c≤b. Lifts x,y have [x,y]=z of order p^c and x^(p^a)=z^d, y^(p^b)=z^e, with (d,e) arbitrary modulo p^c. These presentations are consistent: after imposing the commutator order in the free class-two group, the two remaining relations are central with independent projections to the free abelianization, so they do not decrease the order of z. Changing the basis of the abelianization acts on (d,e) through the two-by-two invertible matrices with upper-right entry divisible by p^(a−b), with a determinant rescaling. The rescaling does not alter this matrix family. The power-law cross terms vanish modulo p^c except when p=2 and a=b=c>0. In the linear case with h=a−b, the two invariants are s=min(v(d),v(e)) and r=min(v(d),h+v(e),c), with v(0)=c. Swaps when h=0, diagonal units, and upper/lower shears give unique valuation pairs s≤r≤min(c,s+h): when v(d)<v(e) a lower shear makes the e valuation equal to v(d); when v(d)>h+v(e) an upper shear brings the d valuation down to h+v(e); independent units normalize the resulting nonzero entries. In the exceptional equal-exponent case let τ=2^(c−1). For minimum valuation below c−1, a swap puts a lower-valuation entry first and a shear kills the other entry using d±τ, of unchanged valuation; unit scaling finishes. When both entries are multiples of τ, their values divided by τ are the coefficients of the quadratic power map dv₁+ev₂+v₁v₂ over F₂ (where d,e now denote the divided values). The two basis orbits are distinguished by whether this map takes value 1 on one or all three nonzero vectors. There are thus c+1 orbits in the exceptional case too, as required for h=0. This checks the count without assuming an odd-prime logarithm at p=2. With e₁=a−b, e₂=b−c, e₃=c, e₄=r, e₅=s, summing the inequalities gives the claimed five factors; c=0 includes the abelian cases and a=b=c=0 the trivial group. Coprime Sylow factors combine with the same generator bound, giving the Euler product. The summatory constant follows directly by summing floor(x/(b²c³d³e⁴)) over positive b,c,d,e and using the convergent dominating sum after division by x. A separate bounded count of weighted integer solutions reproduced degrees 0–19 in Voll, as reported in the review; this checks the expansion, not group exhaustiveness. The packaged code was inspected, not executed.
